title: Vitamin C Serum
body_html:
Clean vitamin C serum for daily AM brightening and antioxidant protection. Built around a triple ascorbic acid complex stabilized with Ferulic Acid, and balanced with calming botanicals for sensitive-skin tolerance. Vegan, fragrance-free.

  • Noticeably brighter, more even skin tone within 2–3 weeks
  • Daily antioxidant protection against environmental dullness
  • Gentle enough for sensitive skin — calming botanicals offset L-AA sting
  • Visible dark spot reduction with consistent AM use

How to use: Apply to clean, dry skin every morning before moisturizer; always follow with SPF — new to L-AA, start every other morning for 1–2 weeks.

What to expect

  • Day 1: Clean antioxidant layer under your SPF. Daily damage defense starts immediately.
  • Week 1–2: Tone looks brighter. Skin feels fresher in the morning.
  • Week 3–4: Day-to-day radiance builds. Makeup sits better.
  • Week 6–8: Established hyperpigmentation visibly softening. L-AA + MAP + ferulic work at multiple layers.

New to pure vitamin C? Start every other morning for 1–2 weeks, then move to daily.

Key ingredients
  • Triple vitamin C (L-Ascorbic Acid + MAP + 3-Glyceryl Ascorbate) — immediate potency plus stable, extended brightening
  • Ferulic Acid — stabilizes vitamin C and amplifies UV antioxidant defense
  • Calendula + Chamomile Extracts — calming botanicals that offset L-AA sensitivity
  • Rice Extract — softens and supports even tone
Who it's for

Label-readers who want a dependable daily vitamin C for antioxidant protection and general brightness. For stubborn hyperpigmentation or multi-active targeting, pick the Vitamin Glow Serum instead.

Free from

No parabens • No sulfates • No synthetic fragrance • No PEGs • No phthalates

Full ingredient list (INCI)

L-Ascorbic Acid, Magnesium Ascorbyl Phosphate, 3-Glyceryl Ascorbate, Ferulic Acid, Rice Extract, Calendula Extract, Chamomile Extract

Size & suggested use

1 fl oz (30ml) · Made in USA. External use only; avoid eye area; discontinue if irritation occurs; store away from direct sunlight.

faq_json.question: What's the difference between Vitamin C Serum and Vitamin Glow Serum?
faq_json.answer: The short answer: Vitamin C Serum is your daily antioxidant and brightening baseline. Vitamin Glow Serum is a multi-active targeted treatment for more specific concerns. Choose Vitamin C Serum if you want a consistent AM serum that defends against environmental damage, maintains even tone, and delivers reliable day-in, day-out brightening. Choose Vitamin Glow Serum if you're dealing with stubborn hyperpigmentation, uneven skin tone, or dullness that needs a more targeted approach — it combines Niacinamide, 3-O-Ethyl Ascorbic Acid, Vitamin E, and Panthenol for a multi-angle brightening effect. The two are also compatible: some people use Vitamin C Serum in the AM and Vitamin Glow Serum in the PM.

faq_json.question: What form of vitamin C is in this serum?
faq_json.answer: This formula uses three forms: L-Ascorbic Acid (the pure, most-studied form of Vitamin C — the one dermatologists most often recommend), Magnesium Ascorbyl Phosphate (MAP), and 3-Glyceryl Ascorbate. L-AA is the gold standard for potency; MAP and 3-Glyceryl Ascorbate are more stable derivatives that convert to active Vitamin C on the skin's surface with gentler delivery. The combination gives you L-AA's proven efficacy plus the staying power and reduced irritation potential of the stable forms.

faq_json.question: Will this irritate sensitive skin?
faq_json.answer: L-Ascorbic Acid can cause temporary tingling or mild sensitivity in some users — particularly those new to pure Vitamin C or those with very reactive skin. We've balanced the formula with Ferulic Acid (which stabilizes the L-AA and helps maintain a skin-comfortable pH) plus calming botanicals — calendula and chamomile — specifically to reduce irritation potential. If your skin is sensitive, we recommend introducing this every other morning for 1–2 weeks before moving to daily use. If you find pure Vitamin C reliably irritates your skin, Vitamin Glow Serum uses 3-O-Ethyl Ascorbic Acid (an ether-stable C derivative) that tends to be better tolerated.

faq_json.question: Is this safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding?
faq_json.answer: Vitamin C serums are generally considered among the safer actives during pregnancy — unlike retinoids, salicylic acid (in high doses), or hydroquinone. This formula does not contain any of those flagged ingredients. That said, we always recommend consulting your OB or midwife before introducing any new skincare active during pregnancy or breastfeeding. They know your individual health picture; we don't.

faq_json.question: How should I use this in my routine?
faq_json.answer: Apply every morning to clean, dry skin before moisturizer. If you're layering serums: thinner, water-based serums go first (like our PDRN Brightening Serum), then this Vitamin C Serum, then a heavier moisturizer or facial oil, then SPF. SPF is non-negotiable in a Vitamin C routine — Vitamin C primes your skin's antioxidant defense, but it is not a substitute for sunscreen. Apply them both.

faq_json.question: Can I use this with retinol?
faq_json.answer: Yes, but separate them by routine. Use Vitamin C Serum in the morning (where it works best — antioxidant protection is most relevant during daytime UV exposure). Use retinol in the evening. Combining them in the same application isn't necessary and can increase irritation. This separation is the standard dermatologist guidance for pairing these two actives.

faq_json.question: How long until I see results?
faq_json.answer: Many users notice a more even, brighter look within 2–3 weeks of consistent AM use. Visible dark spot reduction and more meaningful tone changes typically emerge at the 4–6 week mark. Vitamin C results are cumulative — the longer you use it consistently, the more your skin benefits. Don't give up in week one if your skin is adjusting.
